tracks.title: Come On Home
tracks.story: Fred again.. and Brian Eno built the whole track around the late John Prine's voice, letting his gentle refrain become the title and the hook. Prine died of COVID-19 in 2020, so what sounds like a lullaby is really an elegy — Four Tet released it and called Secret Life the most beautiful album of 2023.

tracks.title: One More Time
tracks.story: Daft Punk legally licensed the obscure disco record and paid royalties for decades — but the money sat with Johns' old label, which claimed it could never find him. In 2021 the LA Times found Eddie Johns living in homeless shelters in Los Angeles, unaware one of the biggest dance songs ever was built from his horns.

tracks.title: Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger
tracks.story: That instantly recognizable robot riff is lifted almost wholesale from an oddball funk jam about a woman shaped like a cola bottle. Kanye West then sampled Daft Punk's version for 'Stronger' in 2007 — making Edwin Birdsong the secret grandfather of two different generations of number-one hits.

tracks.title: Through the Wire
tracks.story: Kanye recorded his verses two weeks after his near-fatal 2002 car crash with his jaw still wired shut — literally rapping through the wire while sampling Chaka Khan singing about going through the fire. The sped-up soul vocal became the calling card that turned a producer into a rapper.

tracks.title: Crazy in Love (feat. Jay-Z)
tracks.sample_title: Are You My Woman (Tell Me So)
tracks.story: Producer Rich Harrison had the Chi-Lites horn loop sitting unused because artists kept telling him it sounded too retro — Beyoncé had the same worry at first. Harrison, nursing a hangover, wrote the hook in about two hours, and the 1970 soul horns became arguably the defining pop fanfare of the 2000s.

tracks.title: Hard Knock Life (Ghetto Anthem)
tracks.story: After lawyers turned him down, Jay-Z personally wrote the rights-holders a letter claiming he'd won a seventh-grade essay contest and been taken to see Annie on Broadway — a story he later admitted he invented. The fabricated childhood memory worked, and orphans singing showtunes became a ghetto anthem.

tracks.title: Can I Kick It?
tracks.story: Tribe borrowed the most laid-back bassline in rock history — and Lou Reed agreed to clear it only on condition that he receive 100% of the song's royalties. Q-Tip confirmed the group never earned a dime from one of their most beloved songs.

tracks.title: The Next Episode
tracks.artist: Dr. Dre feat. Snoop Dogg, Kurupt & Nate Dogg
tracks.story: That menacing G-funk fanfare comes from an easy-listening instrumental conducted by David McCallum — the actor who played Illya Kuryakin in The Man from U.N.C.L.E. and later Ducky on NCIS — produced by sample-god David Axelrod. A TV spy from 1967 quietly soundtracks one of the greatest rap intros ever.

tracks.title: 1 Thing
tracks.story: Producer Rich Harrison heard the Meters track for the first time in May 2004 and built the whole song around a ten-second drum-and-guitar breakdown, layering bongos over Ziggy Modeliste's playing. The result is basically a 1970 New Orleans funk jam with 2005 R&B vocals on top — and it still sounds like the future.

tracks.title: Frontier Psychiatrist
tracks.story: Every deranged vocal line about needing therapy and lying on the couch comes from a 1959 sketch by Canadian TV comedy duo Wayne and Shuster, collaged with an Enoch Light orchestra and dozens of other records. The band later joked that clearing samples is impossible when one of them is a horse whinny.

tracks.title: Praise You
tracks.story: Norman Cook stumbled on the isolated vocal on a bootleg breaks LP at a Camden Market stall. Yarbrough — a civil-rights-era poet and activist — didn't even know what sampling was until her label called; the UK number one arrived during a career lull and introduced her to a whole new generation.

tracks.title: SICKO MODE (feat. Drake)
tracks.story: Travis raps that Miami treats him like he's Uncle Luke — and the beat instantly flips into a sample of Uncle Luke's own Miami bass classic, a sample deployed as a punchline. The track also samples Biggie's 'Gimme the Loot', which itself sampled Onyx, so Onyx still get royalty checks off SICKO MODE.

tracks.title: Paint The Town Red
tracks.story: When told her Bacharach-David classic was driving 2023's biggest rap hit to number one in 19 countries, the 82-year-old legend's reaction was reportedly 'Doja who?' — before saying she was thrilled a brand-new generation would discover her music.

tracks.title: good 4 u
tracks.story: Released with no credit to Paramore, but TikTok mashups made the resemblance so undeniable that Hayley Williams and Josh Farro were retroactively added as songwriters months later. Williams found out when her publisher posted about it and admitted even she was surprised.

tracks.title: Pain
tracks.story: The bedroom-pop breakout that launched PinkPantheress rides a Y2K UK garage classic — except she reportedly sampled a karaoke version of it, and Sweet Female Attitude's own singer said it sounded like one to her ear too. The singer only learned the song existed when her teenage daughter showed her a TikTok.

tracks.title: Workinonit
tracks.sample_title: The Worst Band in the World
tracks.story: Dilla flipped a British art-rock deep cut into the opening statement of Donuts, an album he finished from his hospital bed and released three days before his death. Fourteen years later, 10cc's publishers sued the late producer's estate over the sample — a lawsuit against a man who had been gone since 2006.
